ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Sudden-onset mid-sternal chest “pressure” while digging in the garden (light physical exertion) ≈ 2 h ago; persists.  
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Constant since onset, rated 7/10; unchanged at rest.  
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation – not reported.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness – denied.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia – denied.  
  • Drooling – not reported.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms – none.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing – none.  
  • Dyspnea – present (shortness of breath at rest; longstanding exertional limitation).  
  • Swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face) – none.  
  • Ear or neck symptoms – none.  
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Progressive exertional dyspnea, calf pain, and leg swelling over recent weeks; no prior hospital evaluations; no previous epinephrine or airway intervention.  
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies – not documented.  
  • Regular medications – none.  
  • Rescue medications/devices – none.  
- Social context:
  • Lives with wife; wife present at home and alerted to forthcoming ambulance.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution – none mentioned.  
- Airway/breathing – reports dyspnea; no stridor or audible wheeze described.  
- Mental status – alert, conversant; light-headedness reported.  
- Vitals/exam – Not recorded (remote video consultation).  
- Accompanied – wife at home; paramedics summoned.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Suspected acute coronary syndrome; airway currently stable with no ENT obstruction features.
  Evidence: sudden pressure-type chest pain radiating to left shoulder/arm, dyspnea, nausea, untreated HTN/hyperlipidemia, current smoker.
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with DDx):
  1. Acute coronary syndrome (high likelihood) – classic symptom pattern and risk factors.
  2. Pulmonary embolism (medium likelihood) – acute dyspnea plus history of calf pain/leg swelling; chest pain non-pleuritic (opposing evidence).
  3. Aortic dissection (low–medium) – abrupt chest pain in hypertensive patient; pain described as pressure, no back radiation (opposing evidence).
  (DDx items beyond top 3 omitted for conciseness.)

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Emergency services (ambulance) called; patient instructed to remain on phone until arrival.  
  • Advised to stay calm, sit upright, sip water only if needed; avoid any medications until assessed.  
- Patient/caregiver instructions:
  • Wife to prepare essentials for hospital; accompany patient.  
  • Avoid exertion; monitor for worsening breathlessness, voice change, throat tightness, new swelling, syncope – call EMS if deterioration.  
- Escalation criteria/red flags reiterated: worsening chest pain, dyspnea, fainting, new neck or facial swelling, stridor.  
- Follow-up:
  • Hospital evaluation (ED/consultant review) imminent.  
  • Post-discharge: recommend cardiology ± respiratory follow-up; smoking cessation, hypertension/lipid management.  
  • Consider ENT review only if airway symptoms develop (none currently).

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected elements: complete allergy list, vitals (BP, HR, RR, O2 sat), physical airway/neck exam, medication dose/route if any given, prior anaphylaxis or auto-injector status (not relevant but standard checklist).  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minimal background noise; no significant inaudible segments.
